definition: Open Knowledge Base Connectivity (OKBC) is a protocol and an API for accessing knowledge in knowledge representation systems such as ontology repositories and object–relational databases.
details: It is somewhat complementary to the Knowledge Interchange Format that serves as a general representation language for knowledge. It is developed by SRI International's Artificial Intelligence Center for DARPA's High Performance Knowledge Base program (HPKB).

explainer.lead: OKBC is a protocol and API for accessing knowledge stored in knowledge representation systems such as ontology repositories and object–relational databases. It matters because it gives a uniform way to reach knowledge held in otherwise incompatible stores.

tiers.eli5: It's like a standard plug shape so different knowledge-storing systems can be queried the same way.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use it to query ontologies and databases through one interface instead of writing custom access code per store. Pitfall: it defines access, not the language knowledge is written in, so representation differences remain.
tiers.paperLevel: A protocol plus API specification for accessing knowledge in knowledge representation systems; it is complementary to the Knowledge Interchange Format, a general representation language for knowledge.

explainer.example: A system holds an ontology in one repository and facts in an object–relational database; an OKBC-conformant interface lets an application retrieve knowledge from both.
